product.name: AgentX WebMate
product.description: AI browser agent — chat with pages, automate tasks, multi-provider LLM support.
product._extensionId_why: Fixed Chrome/Edge extension ID, derived from manifestOverrides.chrome.key (SHA-256 of the SPKI public key, first 16 bytes, a-p). Workmate reads extensions.settings[<this id>] in the browser profile to know whether WebMate is installed; scripts/brand-build.mjs fails the build if the two ever disagree. The private half lives outside the repo (~/.agentx/webmate-keys/manifest-key.pem).

mcp._why: Names the MCP server in mcp-server/ derives at build time (scripts/brand.mjs). Every value here equals what product.* would derive on its own; it is spelled out so a brand branch sees exactly which knobs exist. Tools become <toolPrefix>_run/_extract/_status/_respond/_abort/_connection, hosts show them as mcp__<skillName>__<toolPrefix>_*.

services._skillHubBaseUrl_why: AgentX Skill Hub (plan §8 decision 2). Also the only origin allowed to message the extension (externally_connectable, Chrome/Edge) — scripts/brand-build.mjs derives both from this value.

Settings > Skills opens on a paragraph that spells out the WebMCP fence names `webbrain-tools` and `webbrain-skill` inside <code> tags, so the upstream brand reaches the screen however the display-name rules are scoped. Those two are protocol identifiers external sites rely on — they stay put in src/agent/skills.js and in the packaged skills, and only the visible copy can move. Rewriting the whole sentence also sheds the catalog/planner/semantic-intent wording it opened with, which is loader detail nobody reading that tab for the first time needs. One rule per locale, since each carries its own translation; the pattern matches the key and whatever value trails it, so an upstream rewording is swallowed rather than quietly restoring the old text.

manifestOverrides._chrome_why: `key` pins the extension ID whether the folder is loaded unpacked by Workmate or packed for a store; `minimum_chrome_version` 121 is the first Chrome without the developer-mode nag bubble. Firefox (MV2, AMO) gets neither.
manifestOverrides._chrome_addPermissions_why: Union with the upstream permissions (scripts/brand-build.mjs). `identity` is for chrome.identity.launchWebAuthFlow: Workmate's `auth_hint` runs a prompt=none authorize against Keycloak so a browser already signed in to Workmate signs WebMate in without a click (docs/workmate-integration.md, phase 4). The redirect https://<extensionId>.chromiumapp.org/ must be registered on the Keycloak client.

workmate._why: Contract with AgentX Workmate, which installs this extension unpacked from a folder it owns and updates it from release.json (scripts/build-zip.mjs, scripts/sign-release.mjs). installDirName is the folder Chrome is pointed at — Chrome stores the absolute path, so the name never changes between versions. minWorkmate/minProtocol are copied into release.json so an old Workmate does not install an extension it cannot talk to.
